2. The facts of the case, in short, are that respondent No. 1 herein Syed Moinuddin Ahmed as petitioner filed Miscellaneous EC No. 6/1982 under section 36(1) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1963, (the Ordinance), before the Administrator of Waqfs for declaring the disputed property as waqf property, in respect of which a notification was issued under section 34 of the Ordinance, refusing to enlist the property as waqf property. 

 3. That application having been rejected respondent No. 1 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 2/86 before the District Judge, Moulvibazar under section 50 of the Ordinance. 

 4. Upon hearing, the learned District judge by his judgment and order dated 25-1-1997 rejected the petition holding that the property in the schedule to the application has not been dedicated by waqf lillah for the interest of the Jame Masjid of Srimongal. However, instead of filing an appeal before the High Court Division, respondent No. 1 herein filed Civil Revision No. 3123 of 1997 and obtained Rule, which upon hearing was discharged with the direction to file a proper appeal. Hence, opposite Party No. 1 in the civil revision as petitioner filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1103 of 2015 before this Division and leave was granted to consider the following submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. "That the High Court Division failed to take into consideration that the order dated 25-1-1997 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 1986 by the District Judge, Moulvibazar, is an order appealable within 60 days under section 35(3) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962. The period for filing an appeal having been provided under special law, the delay cannot be condoned, particularly since the revision before the High Court Division was itself filed beyond the period of limitation prescribed for appeal." 

 6. Mrs Jaya Bhattacharjee, learned Advocate appearing for respondent No. 1 made submissions in support of the impugned observation, direction and status-quo of the High Court Division. She also submitted that in view of the circumstances in the present case, the provision of section 14 of the Limitation Act read with section 5 is applicable and hence, the High Court Division did not commit any error of law in giving the respondents herein a chance to file an appeal against the judgment and order passed by the District Judge and thus the appeal is liable to be dismissed. She submitted that earlier Humayun Bakth Chowdhury filed a petition before the Settlement Circle Officer, Srimongal as Petition Case No. 354 of 1958 and submitted that as the land was given to the mosque verbally by Muzaffar Bakth Chowdhury and his son does not want to take away the land from the mosque, it should be recorded in the name of the masjid committee under Humayun Bakth Chowdhury and the said petition was allowed on 5-11-1958 and these appellants were present before the Court but against the said judgment, no appeal was filed by the present appellants, i.e. second party and thus the instant appeal is liable to be dismissed for ends of justice. 

 10. However, the difficulty in the instant case is that the revisional application was filed before the High Court Division admittedly after delay of 9 days with a prayer for condonation of delay. The High Court Division in the impugned judgment directed the petitioner in the civil revision to file an appeal in accordance with law but failed to consider that such appeal would be beyond the period of limitation since the revision was admittedly filed 9 days after the period of limitation had expired. 

 12. In the facts and circumstance mentioned above, therefore, the direction to file appeal before the High Court Division is misconceived since such appeal would automatically be barred by limitation.
